lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is a public vote on who leads Telluride Regional Medical Center — the board goes into executive session and then takes public action on interim hospital leadership, and public comment is open via Zoom. Right behind that, Town Council takes up a deed-restriction amendment that would remove the sale-price cap on two affordable units at 215 East Colorado Avenue, which is the kind of structural housing change that's hard to undo. Mountain Village is also moving a first reading that shifts how affordable housing fees get set, and the Telluride P&Z holds a work session on the Comprehensive Plan update with a second community survey in play.

notable.stake: Board votes publicly on who runs the hospital; public comment open.
Vote could remove price cap on two affordable units, shrinking protected stock.
Resolution converts two ownership units to EDUs, removing maximum sale price.
First reading shifts affordable housing fee-setting authority out of municipal code.
Comp Plan update shapes long-term land use and density; Survey 2 presented.
